answer: The exciseman brands every still with his own mark and logs each run in the still book, and no cask may leave the glen unless its run is written down. A reef cask filled from an unbranded still fails the mark: the relic of the still must match the exciseman's own brand, and an unbranded cask smells of a hidden bothy. Forging the run means keeping a still for a season, distilling 90 gallons and paying 16,400, while the ocean entry in the still book is read by the exciseman each month, so a cask whose run was never logged is smashed on the shore.
